correctness.rationale: Re-audited /workspace/repairs/5/. The original maximality argument for a proper bridge asserted incompatible phases after extension, but p-apart starts can share a phase; it is the insufficient length of any putative mixed border that prevents closedness. The repair proves both extensions stay in same-letter runs. Every unary border of either extension has length at most t, occurs twice or more in its enlarged end-run and at least once at the other end. A mixed witness must have starts exactly p apart, by its unique phase and the intervening-copy argument, so its length would be 2t+1−ℓ≤t and it would be unary when this length is positive. For t=ℓ one can add a following 1 to a zero bridge or a preceding 0 to a one bridge, yielding a complete return to a mixed border at shift p. Mixed-border witnesses at shift p extend wherever available, leaving only the full word; unary maximal factors are exactly the full runs. The three disjoint families therefore give (k−1)p+3. For a cut inside a run of length ℓ at offset u, incoming and outgoing same-symbol bridge contributions are bounded by ℓ−1−u and u−1, leaving room for that run's unique crossing occurrence. At a run boundary no run crosses and at most one pair per symbol can contribute. The whole interval contributes one at every cut, and both symbols' full bridge families cross each c=mp, attaining p−1. This includes unit runs (no same-symbol bridges) and finite word endpoints; the all-k result is symbolic. Independent corroboration: python /workspace/branches/mcs_independent.py (216 instances with 1≤a,b≤6 and 2≤k≤7). It computes the longest proper border by the prefix function and checks for an earlier overlapping repeat before the suffix. This suffices: any shorter border has an extra occurrence ending at the end of a longer proper prefix border. Frozen scripts and logs were inspected, not run.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Equal same-symbol run heights make visibility equivalent to adjacency, and equal right flanks for zero-runs or equal left flanks for one-runs remove the full-run length. The published RLE results supply much more than an instance-specific algorithm; this review credits the bridge classification as a direct specialization. The unrestricted cut bounds neither specialize to p−1 for length kp nor characterize where it is attained.

Neither a generic cut bound nor an occurrence list alone gives those assertions without this additional analysis.

value.rationale: Uniform equal-block powers are a natural compressed input model for internal reporting. The sharp worst local output depends on the period alone, independent of k, while the total grows linearly in k; this contrast and the equality locations give a distinct structural benchmark not supplied by the generic n-dependent bound. The local bridge/run tradeoff, rather than merely re-running an enumerator or counting known families globally, is the point of the repaired contribution.
